name: IN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+15 partisan lean in a heavily Republican district
Incumbent Jim Baird running with large fundraising and outside support edge
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Baird's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage leave Cox with no visible path; markets agree at roughly 94% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings to move the forecast, the baseline stands.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge against Baird or an unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the race, though the lean makes that unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Indiana's 4th District is a heavily Republican seat with a partisan lean of about R+15, and incumbent Jim Baird is running for another term after easily securing renomination. His challenger, Democrat Drew Cox, has raised only about $20,000 and had under $7,000 on hand, while Baird has raised roughly $358,000 and benefits from over $500,000 in outside support, though about $200,000 in outside spending opposes him. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets put Baird's chances at about 94%. The combination of the district's lean, incumbency, and the large resource gap makes this a Safe Republican race, with only modest uncertainty from the absence of polling.
